arxiv-2203-07160.creator: Ye Huang, Di Kang, Liang Chen, Xuefei Zhe, Wenjing Jia, Linchao Bao, Xiangjian He
arxiv-2203-07160.description: Abstract Recent segmentation methods, such as OCR and CPNet, utilizing “class level” information in addition to pixel features, have achieved notable success for boosting the accuracy of existing network modules. However, the extracted class-level information was simply concatenated to pixel features, without explicitly being exploited for better pixel representation learning.

arxiv-2410-07971.title: Generalizable and Animatable Gaussian Head Avatar
arxiv-2410-07971.creator: Xuangeng Chu, Tatsuya Harada
arxiv-2410-07971.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose G eneralizable and A nimatable G aussian head A vatar (GAGAvatar) for one-shot animatable head avatar reconstruction. Existing methods rely on neural radiance fields, leading to heavy rendering consumption and low reenactment speeds. To address these limitations, we generate the parameters of 3D Gaussians from a single image in a single forward pass.

arxiv-2501-17133.title: Ultrafast and compact photonic-electronic leaky integrate-and-fire circuits based upon resonant tunnelling diodes Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2501-17133.creator: Joshua Robertson, 1,* Dylan Black, 1 Giovanni Donati, 1 Qusay Raghib Ali Al-Taai, 2 Ekaterina Malysheva, 3 Bruno Romeira, 4 José Figueiredo, 5 Victor Dolores Calzadilla, 3 Edward Wasige, 2 and Antonio Hurtado 1
arxiv-2501-17133.description: Abstract This work provides a first report of ultrafast and compact photonic-electronic neuromorphic temporal leaky integrate-and-fire neuronal circuits built with Resonant Tunnelling Diodes (RTDs). We demonstrate experimentally that multiple fast ( ∼ \sim 100-200 ps) optical input pulses, arriving within a short (sub-ns long) temporal window, control the triggering of excitable responses in two different photonic-electronic RTD circuit architectures.

arxiv-2512-13609.title: Do-Undo: Generating and Reversing Physical Actions in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2512-13609.creator: Shweta Mahajan, Shreya Kadambi, Hoang Le, Munawar Hayat, Fatih Porikli
arxiv-2512-13609.description: Abstract We introduce the Do-Undo task and benchmark to address a critical gap in vision-language models: understanding and generating physically plausible scene transformations driven by real-world actions. Unlike prior work focused on object-level edits, Do-Undo requires models to simulate the outcome of a physical action and then accurately reverse it, reflecting true cause-and-effect in the visual world.

pmc-10671328.title: Predisposition of the Common MC4R rs17782313 Female Carriers to Elevated Obesity and Interaction with Eating Habits
pmc-10671328.creator: Danyel Chermon, Ruth Birk
pmc-10671328.description: The global rise in obesity is attributed to genetic predisposition interaction with an obesogenic environment. Melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) rs17782313 polymorphism has been linked to common obesity with varying influence across different populations. MC4R is a crucial player in the leptin proopiomelanocortin pathway that regulates weight hemostasis.

pmc-10719857.title: I don’t understand how I feel: mediating role of impaired self-mentalizing in the relationship between childhood adversity and psychosis spectrum experiences
pmc-10719857.creator: Jacqueline Nonweiler, Pilar Torrecilla, Thomas R. Kwapil, Sergi Ballespí, Neus Barrantes-Vidal
pmc-10719857.description: IntroductionChildhood adversity is associated with the severity of multiple dimensions of psychosis, but the mechanisms underpinning the close link between the two constructs is unclear. Mentalization may underlie this relationship, as impaired mentalizing is found in various stages of the psychosis continuum. Nonetheless, the differential roles of self- and other-mentalizing in psychosis are not well understood.

pmc-11577487.description: ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to assess the knowledge and awareness of guided dentistry among various dental professionals. pmc-12449594.title: Diagnostic Performance of Fibrosis‐4 Index, Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Fibrosis Score, AST‐To‐Platelet Ratio Index, and BARD Score Among Young and Older Adults for the Diagnosis of Advanced MASLD Fibrosis: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-12449594.creator: Frank Lin, Ayah Obeid, Mehak Sharma, Parampreet Kaur, Kimberly Chaput, Hammad Liaquat
pmc-12449594.description: AimsThis study aims to compare the diagnostic performance and accuracy of non‐invasive fibrosis scoring tools, including the Fibrosis‐4 index (Fib‐4), Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Fibrosis Score (NFS), AST‐to‐Platelet Ratio Index (APRI), and BARD score among patients with biopsy‐proven MASLD or MASH, to either diagnose or exclude advanced fibrosis.

pmc-12800193.title: An ethnic-sensitive hybrid framework for T2D prediction with explainable AI and weighted ensembles
pmc-12800193.creator: Karlo Abnoosian, Rahman Farnoosh, Hamidreza Noushkaran, Danial Javaheri, Hasnat Azeez Shimal, Abdullah Abdulamer Abdulkarem
pmc-12800193.description: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a growing global health crisis, affecting over 537 million people as of 2021. Early prediction remains particularly challenging in low- and middle-income countries due to missing data, class imbalance, and population-specific risk factors. This study presents a four-stage predictive framework— Feature-Weighted Class-Adaptive Generative Imputation Network-Weighted Classifier Aggregation Ensemble (FW-CAGIN-WCAE)—designed to address these limitations.

pmc-12849253.title: Perceived organizational status and bootleg innovation: the role of moral licensing in breaking rules
pmc-12849253.creator: Du-Juan Huang, Xi-Ou Gao, Wei Shao, Jun-Ru Wang
pmc-12849253.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundBootleg innovation differs from traditional innovation in that it involves actions that either contravene established organizational rules and procedures or are conducted autonomously and covertly by individuals, with the aim of benefiting the organization. While prior research has highlighted a strong link between moral factors and bootleg innovation, there remains a paucity of studies exploring the moral foundations underlying such innovation.

pmc-13059763.title: mGem: Applying microbiome therapeutic learnings to next-generation agricultural bioproducts
pmc-13059763.creator: Eric C. Holmes
pmc-13059763.description: Biological discoveries in plant and human systems have long advanced our understanding of how signaling, metabolism, and immunity shape cross-kingdom interactions. Building on this rich history of interdisciplinary insight, there is now a tremendous opportunity to strengthen connections between human and agricultural microbiome research.

pmc-13275921.title: The role of protein quality in designing sustainable food systems
pmc-13275921.creator: Shiksha Adhikari, Ollie van Hal, Benjamin van Selm, Thom Huppertz, Imke J. M. de Boer
pmc-13275921.description: The influence of protein digestibility and the adequacy of indispensable amino acids (IAAs) on designing sustainable food systems is not yet fully understood. In this study, we used FOODSOM (FOOD Systems Optimization Model) to evaluate the effects of including total or digestible protein and IAA requirements on land use and dietary outcomes of the Dutch food system.

pmc-13436315.title: Co-application of biochar and cow manure enhances growth, yield and soil chemical properties under spinach production
pmc-13436315.creator: Cosmas Wacal, Ronald Buwa, Jackson Nyakahuma, Patrick Kirungi, Thaddeo Kahigwa Tibasiima, Jacob Kaingo, Deogratius Luyima, Joseph Okello, Geoffrey Levuason Candia, Bruce Robin Nyamweha
pmc-13436315.description: BackgroundDeclining soil fertility remains a major constraint to vegetable production in tropical regions, necessitating sustainable and efficient nutrient management strategies. This study evaluated the effects of biochar, cow manure and their co-application on growth, yield and soil chemical properties of spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.) under field conditions in western Uganda.

pmc-13506283.title: Extracurricular activities as a moderator of the association between screen time and executive functions in children
pmc-13506283.creator: Elena Chichinina, Anastasia Yakushina, Maria Dmitrieva, Natalia Rudnova, Aleksander Pashenko, Suncica Pocek, Patrik Drid
pmc-13506283.description: IntroductionScreen time and extracurricular activities represent two prominent components of modern childhood, particularly among children aged 6–7 years. Given the landscape, the aim of this study was to examine whether the number of different extracurricular activities attended by a child moderates the association between screen time and executive functions in children aged 6–7 years.
